newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 15.0/16.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 15.0/16.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 15.0/16.0 percent on Thursday morning, but operators' focus was on likely liquidity conditions on Friday, dealers said.
They said overnight money was relatively high following a small injection by the central bank early in the morning.
But the focus was on Friday as operators speculated that tight conditions were likely, as on the last three Fridays.
Dealers said the underlying worry was reflected by soaring tom/next swap rate, which rose to 2.3/2.8 from 1.9/2.0 points.
One foreign bank dealer said fears of a tight market heated up after some state banks were seen absorbing rupiah from the market on Wednesday.
Other dealers said rises in short-term money seemed to have also driven longer-term maturities to follow, with one-week money over tomorrow hitting 14.5 percent against 13.5/14.0 percent previously.
One-month money was quoted at 14.50/14.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 11.84 percent, compared with 13.95 percent on Tuesday.
